meta.paired_boundary: Do not relax thresholds, delete failures, change definitions, or test only favorable conditions.

objective_breakdown: Energy density >=392.61 Wh/kg; 4C charge at 45C without plating; T_max <=333.15 K; overcharge to 4.7 V without thermal runaway. ED/thermal/rate trade off.
candidate_strategy: Characterize Chen2020 baseline, then evaluate LNMO 4.7-V-class system and architecture/transport variants; use coupled safety and abuse protocols.
budget_allocation: SPMe screen then DFN for finalists; safety for finalist; no true compute.
risk_and_fallback: Route ED ceiling/material voltage failures to system/material scale; route plating/temperature to architecture, transport, particle size, and cooling. Three strikes trigger reachability questioning.

detail: Stage 3 start; molecular funnel skipped. Chen2020 baseline materials used directly with source=baseline. Chosen base verified by default mapping because no electrode system was named.

recommendation: Not achieved within the executed virtual-design budget. The LNMO high-voltage system achieved 420.26697755476647 Wh/kg and no thermal runaway in the overcharge ODE, and the transport/cooling variant reduced 4C T_max to 327.9222725028953 K. However, every executed LNMO 4C safety run mechanically reported lithium plating (minimum anode potential below 0 V), so the complete contract is not met. The blocking issue is 4C plating at 45 C, not energy density or overcharge runaway.

questions.conclusion: The LNMO model is physically capable of the ED and overcharge targets and its temperature is controllable, but the configured 4C/45 C charge remains plating-limited.
questions.why continue/stop: Do not claim achievement; a different anode/electrolyte chemistry or a lower fast-charge current would be needed.

questions.conclusion: The widest boundary was executed: electrolyte transport, particle size, and cooling were adjustable. No additional unmodeled lever was silently assumed.
questions.why continue/stop: Further tuning of the same transport/cooling direction is not justified after persistent plating.

questions.conclusion: The exact no-plating requirement is retained; it is not relaxed. Within the tested LNMO boundary the full objective is not demonstrated.
questions.why continue/stop: Close honestly as negative rather than convert a plating failure into a pass.
